Frozen WoRMS lineage for the ICES example data

Source: R/data.R
ices_lineage.Rd

The taxonomic lineage (kingdom to species) of every AphiaID in ices_diet, as resolved in WoRMS. Pass it to dv_prepare() with taxonomy = "table": its key column, prey_aphia_id, has the same name as the prey key of ices_diet. A taxon that is itself above species (e.g. "Crustacea", a subphylum) has NA at the finer ranks, which DietView shows as the unidentified share of that branch. WoRMS gives no order to some polychaetes and lancelets and no class to Priapulida, so a few records identified to family or species also reach an NA node at those ranks.

Usage

ices_lineage

Format

A data frame with 461 rows and 10 columns: prey_aphia_id, scientific_name, worms_rank (the WoRMS rank of the name), then the seven ranks kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.

Source

World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS, https://www.marinespecies.org), as compiled in the R package stomachr (Lindmark 2026); kingdom and species columns derived from the WoRMS phylum and the name's rank.

Examples

ices_lineage[ices_lineage$scientific_name %in% c("Crustacea", "Crangon crangon"), ]
#>    prey_aphia_id scientific_name worms_rank  kingdom     phylum        class
#> 48        107552 Crangon crangon    Species Animalia Arthropoda Malacostraca
#> 77          1066       Crustacea  Subphylum Animalia Arthropoda         <NA>
#>       order      family   genus         species
#> 48 Decapoda Crangonidae Crangon Crangon crangon
#> 77     <NA>        <NA>    <NA>            <NA>
